evidence.text: Represents heaven (天), earth (旦), or the number 1
A single horizontal stroke, representing the number one.
惟初太始，道立於一，造分天地，化成萬物。凡一之屬皆从一。

Ideogram (指事): a horizontal stroke, indicating the number “one”.
From Proto-Sino-Tibetan *ʔit. Descendants from the *ʔit etymon account for the majority of the dialectal forms for “one” in Chinese (Mandarin, Jin, Gan, Hakka, Hui, Xiang, Yue, Wu groups, etc.).

Form used as the colloquial reading for “one” in most Min varieties: Fuzhou/Fuding suoʔ⁸, Fuqing θyo⁸, Gutian syøʔ⁸, Ningde søʔ⁸, Zhouning sɔʔ⁸, Putian ɬoʔ⁸, Xiamen/Quanzhou/Yongchun/Zhangzhou tsit̚⁸, Leizhou/Haikou ziak⁸, Longyan tse⁴, Youxi ɕie⁷, Jian'ou/Songxi tsi⁵, Jianyang tsi⁸. Whether all of the forms above are related and their origins remain unelucidated; they may be derived from 蜀 (shǔ) (cf. 獨 /独 (dú, “single, alone”); often written when read with the colloquial reading), 隻 /只 (zhī) (< *kV-tek) or 禃 (zhí). Some Fujian dialects use 個 /个 and 寡 (guǎ) for “one”.
Contraction of 一個 /一个 (yīgè) (Zhou, 1998).

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Etymology Database, CUHK)
evidence.text: The entry reports oracle-bone 一 used as a numeral and gives the example 《合集》21575「一牛」 (‘one ox’). This supports an early numeric use, but the accessible result does not provide a date for that inscription.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — Oracle-bone entry for 一

evidence.source: 說文解字在線查詢 Shuowen.org
evidence.field: 一 entry; seal form and historical explanation
evidence.text: The entry prints the received Shuowen definition 惟初太始，道立於一，造分天地，化成萬物 and says forms in the 一 category derive from 一. It also labels 弌 as 古文一. This is a Han lexicographic and cosmological account, not independent proof of the graph’s earliest origin. The page includes Duan Yucai’s later note classifying 一 as an indicative graph, which is an interpretive classification rather than paleographic evidence.
evidence.title: 說文解字「一」

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart, supplementary materials for Old Chinese: A New Reconstruction
evidence.text: The table lists 一 with Mandarin yī, Middle Chinese 'jit (with its analysis), Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *ʔi[t], gloss ‘one’, and GSR 0394a. The local row in sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv agrees exactly: MC 'jit and OC *ʔi[t]. The modern Mandarin and reconstructed historical forms are readings of the character/word, not evidence for a graphic component or borrowing.

evidence.field: 形義源流通解; 一 entry
evidence.text: The entry says oracle-bone and bronze forms represent the concept of one with an abstract horizontal stroke, and that these forms and the small-seal form use one horizontal stroke for the number one. It cites oracle-bone 《合集》21575「一牛」 as a numeral use. The page also discusses 弌 as a more complex form: it reports the received Shuowen label 古文一, then gives a later proposal deriving the shape through 戈 and 一, and marks the suggested 戌-based precursor as unattested and tentative. This is a source account, not independent verification of every proposed graphic transition.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.
